List the collection of a user

Source: R/users.R
dig_collection.Rd

Lists the releases in the collection of a 'Discogs' user. Anyone can read a public collection. A private collection can only be read with the token of its owner, see dig_auth(). Without a username, the collection of the token owner is listed.

Usage

dig_collection(
  username = NULL,
  folder = 0,
  sort = c("added", "artist", "title", "label", "catno", "format", "rating", "year"),
  order = c("asc", "desc"),
  all = FALSE,
  page = 1,
  per_page = 50
)

Arguments

username

A 'Discogs' username, or NULL for the owner of the token set with dig_auth(). Finding the owner takes one request, once per session.

folder

The ID of a collection folder, see dig_collection_folders(). The default, 0, holds the whole collection and is the only folder other users can read.

sort

The column to sort by: "added", "artist", "title", "label", "catno", "format", "rating" or "year".

order

The sort order: "asc" or "desc".

all

If TRUE, all pages are fetched and page and per_page are ignored.

page

The page to fetch.

per_page

The number of items per page, from 1 to 100.

Value

A tibble with one row per copy of a release, or NULL invisibly if the API cannot be reached. The columns are release_id, instance_id, folder_id, title, artist, year, label, catno, format, media_condition, sleeve_condition, genres and styles as list columns, master_id, rating and date_added. rating is NA if the user gave none. The conditions are factors from best to worst, with the same grades as dig_price_suggestions(). The sleeve condition can also be "Generic" or "No Cover", and a condition is NA if the user gave none.

Details

A release that is in the collection more than once has one row per copy, each with its own instance_id. Collections are never cached, so changes show up at once.

The media and sleeve conditions come from the collection fields named Media and Sleeve. If any copy has a value in a field, the fields are matched by name with one more request. Other fields, such as Notes, are left out. Without the token of the owner, only public fields can be read, and the conditions are NA for fields that are private. If the fields cannot be read, a message says so and the conditions are NA.

Restricted Data

Collections, wantlists, usernames and marketplace data, such as prices and collection values, are Restricted Data under the 'Discogs' API Terms of Use. 'Discogs' grants each user a limited, personal licence to access and use them with their own token. They may not be passed on to anyone else or used for commercial purposes, and their use must respect the privacy of their owners. Keep them, and tallies and plots of them, for your own use, and do not publish them. The Terms of Use also forbid using the API to get around the 'Discogs' marketplace.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
collection <- dig_collection("username", all = TRUE)
dplyr::count(collection, format, sort = TRUE)
dplyr::count(collection, media_condition)
}
